issues.legal_issue: A plaint that does not disclose a cause of action or triable issue must be rejected even if the trial court has issued summons.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought to invalidate a consent decree after accepting the benefits under it.
The plaintiff did not allege fraud, coercion, or misrepresentation, but relied on asserted defects in the earlier proceedings.
The challenged firm’s description had been allowed to be corrected, the plaintiff represented the correctly identified firm throughout, and no distinct entity was claimed.
No relief had been sought or granted against the formal party said not to have been discharged by the decree.
The compromise records showed payment to the relevant party and a sale deed, contrary to the allegation that there was no consideration for relinquishing that party’s interest.
The asserted grounds did not disclose a cause of action or raise a triable issue, although the trial court had issued summons.
issues.conclusion: The plaint was liable to be rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Issuance of summons did not require the trial to proceed where no triable issue arose. The Court rejected the plaint without deciding whether Order 23 Rule 3A applied.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a plaint that does not disclose a cause of action is liable to be rejected. Issuance of summons does not cure that defect or require a trial to continue where no triable issue is shown. The Court did not decide the applicability of Order 23 Rule 3A and cited no earlier cases as authority.

rule.if: suit_challenges_consent_decree_after_benefits_taken and no_fraud_coercion_or_misrepresentation_alleged and firm_description_did_not_identify_a_distinct_entity and no_relief_was_sought_or_granted_against_formal_party and compromise_records_showed_consideration and summons_issued_without_triable_issue_shown

predicates.suit_challenges_consent_decree_after_ben: The plaintiff sought to set aside a consent decree after taking the benefits available under it.
predicates.no_fraud_coercion_or_misrepresentation_a: The plaintiff did not allege that the decree resulted from fraud, coercion, or misrepresentation.
predicates.firm_description_did_not_identify_a_dist: The plaintiff relied on a firm’s incomplete description but did not claim that it referred to a legal entity distinct from the firm correctly represented throughout the proceedings.
predicates.no_relief_was_sought_or_granted_against_: The plaintiff relied on the failure expressly to discharge a party against whom no relief had been sought or granted.
predicates.compromise_records_showed_consideration: The compromise records showed payment and a transfer of interest, despite the plaintiff’s allegation that there was no consideration for relinquishment.
predicates.summons_issued_without_triable_issue_sho: The trial court issued summons even though the pleaded grounds did not show a triable issue.

issues.definition: When a suit challenges a consent decree after its benefits have been taken, the pleaded grounds are contradicted by the record and do not show a triable issue, the plaint is rejected for absence of a cause of action notwithstanding the issuance of summons.

issues.legal_issue: A belated proposed amendment may be refused when it seeks to add grounds already concluded by a final prior adjudication and is aimed at avoiding rejection of the plaint.
material_facts: During the appeal, the plaintiff sought to amend the plaint to add grounds that had been raised and rejected in earlier proceedings concerning the decree.
The application was highly belated and was made after the absence of a cause of action had been identified as requiring rejection of the plaint.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused the application to amend the plaint because it was a belated afterthought and the proposed grounds had already been concluded by the earlier final adjudication.
issues.legal_principle: The Court refused the amendment in light of its lateness, its apparent purpose of avoiding rejection of the plaint, and the fact that the proposed grounds had been concluded by the earlier adjudication. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case as authority for this ruling.

rule.if: appeal_from_suit_maintainability_order and amendment_sought_during_appeal and amendment_is_highly_belated and proposed_grounds_were_concluded_by_final_prior_adjudication and amendment_aims_to_avoid_plaint_rejection

predicates.appeal_from_suit_maintainability_order: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a lower court’s ruling that a suit is maintainable.
predicates.amendment_sought_during_appeal: The plaintiff applied to amend the plaint while the appeal was being heard.
predicates.amendment_is_highly_belated: The plaintiff sought the amendment only after the case had advanced to the appeal stage.
predicates.proposed_grounds_were_concluded_by_final: The grounds proposed for addition had already been rejected in an earlier adjudication that had become final.
predicates.amendment_aims_to_avoid_plaint_rejection: The proposed amendment was an afterthought intended to avert rejection of the plaint for failure to disclose a cause of action.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks a highly belated amendment during an appeal concerning maintainability to add grounds already finally decided, in an effort to avoid rejection of the plaint, the amendment is denied.
